agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# genact - a nonsense activity generator

**Pretend to be busy or waiting for your computer when you should actually be doing real work!** Impress people with your insane multitasking skills. Just open a few instances of `genact` and watch the show. `genact` has multiple scenes that pretend to be doing something exciting or useful when in reality nothing is happening at all.

![](gifs/cc.gif)
![](gifs/memdump.gif)
![](gifs/cargo.gif)

## Installation

You don't have to install anything! For your convenience, prebuilt binaries for Linux, OSX and Windows are provided that should run without any dependencies. **Additionally, there is a web version available.**

It's compatible with FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, Windows, and most modern web browsers that support WebAssembly.

**On FreeBSD**: You can install via package manager:

    pkg install genact

_genact() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="genact"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        genact)
            opts="-l -m -s -i -h -V --list-modules --modules --speed-factor --instant-print-lines --inhibit --exit-after-time --exit-after-modules --print-completions --print-manpage --help --version"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --modules)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "ansible bootlog botnet bruteforce cargo cc composer cryptomining docker_build docker_image_rm download julia kernel_compile memdump mkinitcpio rkhunter simcity terraform uv weblog wpt" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -m)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "ansible bootlog botnet bruteforce cargo cc composer cryptomining docker_build docker_image_rm download julia kernel_compile memdump mkinitcpio rkhunter simcity terraform uv weblog wpt" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --speed-factor)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -s)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --instant-print-lines)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0

                    return 0

                --exit-after-time)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --exit-after-modules)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --print-completions)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "bash elvish fish powershell zsh" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                *)
                    COMPREPLY=()
                    ;;
            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

import subprocess, time, signal, os

for sig, name in [(signal.SIGTERM, "TERM"), (signal.SIGINT, "INT")]:

    time.sleep(0.5)

    try:

        print(f"{name}: exit={p.returncode} out_len={len(out)} err_len={len(err)}")

        print("  err:", err[:500].decode(errors='replace') if err else "")

        print(f"{name}: TIMEOUT, killing")
        p.kill()
        out,err=p.communicate()

time.sleep(0.5)
p.kill()
out,err=p.communicate(timeout=3)
print(f"KILL: exit={p.returncode} out_len={len(out)} err_len={len(err)}")
print("  out tail:", out[-200:].decode(errors='replace') if out else "")
PY

"}

import pty, os, subprocess, time, struct, fcntl, termios
def run(m, cols, speed="100", timeout=4):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, cols, 0, 0))
    proc = subprocess.Popen(["./executable","-m",m,"--speed-factor",speed],
        stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    out=b""
    start=time.time()
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            break
        try:
            d=os.read(master, 8192)
            if d: out+=d
        except BlockingIOError:
            time.sleep(0.05)
        except: break
    if proc.poll() is None:
        proc.terminate()
        try: proc.wait(timeout=2)
        except: proc.kill()
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 8192)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except: break
        except: pass
    os.close(master)
    txt=out.decode(errors='replace')
    # for ansible, get first PLAY line
    lines=txt.splitlines()
    print(f"m={m} cols={cols} len={len(out)} lines={len(lines)}")
    for l in lines[:5]:
        # strip \r
        print(f"  len={len(l)} {repr(l[:120])}")
    print("---")

for cols in [40,80,120]:
    run("ansible", cols, "100", 3)

pub struct Width(pub u16);
pub struct Height(pub u16);

pub fn terminal_size() -> Option<(Width, Height)> {
    terminal_size_of(libc::STDOUT_FILENO)
}

pub fn terminal_size_of(fd: libc::c_int) -> Option<(Width, Height)> {
    unsafe {
        let mut winsize: libc::winsize = std::mem::zeroed();
        if libc::ioctl(fd, libc::TIOCGWINSZ, &mut winsize) == 0 {
            if winsize.ws_col > 0 && winsize.ws_row > 0 {
                return Some((Width(winsize.ws_col), Height(winsize.ws_row)));
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

pub fn terminal_size_of(fd: libc::c_int) -> Option<(Width, Height)> {
    unsafe {
        let mut ws: libc::winsize = std::mem::zeroed();
        if libc::ioctl(fd, libc::TIOCGWINSZ, &mut ws) == 0 {
            if ws.ws_col > 0 && ws.ws_row > 0 {

fn print_fake_backtrace(frames: usize) {
    let pid = std::process::id() as u64;
    let base: u64 = 0x555500000000u64.wrapping_add((pid.wrapping_mul(0x1a2b3c) & 0xffffff).wrapping_mul(0x1000)) | 0xd00000;
    let offsets: &[u64] = &[0x4b0e2, 0x19c71f, 0x4aabcf, 0x4aaf43, 0x4aa5b0, 0x471015, 0x470fa9, 0x470f9c, 0x19d4bf, 0x1c8e32, 0x1c87c2, 0x12496a, 0x11e618, 0x11b6f7, 0x125435, 0x11b625];
    for idx in 0..frames {
        let (addr_str, suffix) = if idx == frames - 1 {
            (format!("{:#x}", 0), " - <unknown>")
        } else if idx == frames - 2 {
            let libc_base: u64 = 0x7f0000000000u64.wrapping_add((pid.wrapping_mul(0x1000) & 0xffffff000));
            let a = (libc_base & 0x7fff00000000) | 0x33faee40u64 | ((pid & 0xff) << 16);
            (format!("{:#x}", a), " - __libc_start_main")
        } else if idx == frames - 3 {
            let libc_base: u64 = 0x7f0000000000u64.wrapping_add((pid.wrapping_mul(0x1000) & 0xffffff000));
            let a = (libc_base & 0x7fff00000000) | 0x33faed90u64 | ((pid & 0xff) << 16);
            (format!("{:#x}", a), " - <unknown>")
        } else {
            let off = offsets[idx % offsets.len()];
            let a = base.wrapping_add(off).wrapping_add(idx as u64 * 0x10);
            (format!("{:#x}", a), " - <unknown>")
        };
        let padded = format!("{:>19}", addr_str);
        if idx < 10 {
            eprintln!("   {}:{}{}", idx, padded, suffix);
        } else {
            eprintln!("  {}:{}{}", idx, padded, suffix);
        }
    }

all_tasks=set()
for trial in range(3):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    proc = subprocess.Popen(["./executable","-m","ansible","--exit-after-modules","1","--speed-factor","1000"],
        stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    out=b""
    start=time.time()
    while time.time()-start < 10:
        if proc.poll() is not None:
            try:
                while True:
                    try:
                        d=os.read(master, 8192)
                        if not d: break
                        out+=d
                    except BlockingIOError: break
            except: break
            break
        try:
            d=os.read(master, 8192)
            if d: out+=d
        except BlockingIOError:
            time.sleep(0.05)
        except: break
    if proc.poll() is None:
        proc.terminate()
        try: proc.wait(timeout=2)
        except: proc.kill()
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    orig=out.replace(b"\r\r\n", b"\r\n")
    txt=orig.decode(errors='replace')
    tasks=re.findall(r"TASK \[(.*?)\]", txt)
    for t in tasks:
        all_tasks.add(t)
    print(f"trial {trial}: {len(tasks)} tasks")
print(f"total unique {len(all_tasks)}")
for t in sorted(all_tasks)[:100]:
    print(repr(t))

mod humantime;

use clap::{Command, Arg, ArgAction, value_parser};
use std::io::Write;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

fn cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("genact")
        .version("1.5.1")
        .about("A nonsense activity generator")
        .author("Sven-Hendrik Haase <svenstaro@gmail.com>")
        .arg(Arg::new("list-modules").short('l').long("list-modules").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("List available modules"))
        .arg(Arg::new("modules").short('m').long("modules").value_name("MODULES").action(ArgAction::Append).value_parser(["ansible","bootlog","botnet","bruteforce","cargo","cc","composer","cryptomining","docker_build","docker_image_rm","download","julia","kernel_compile","memdump","mkinitcpio","rkhunter","simcity","terraform","uv","weblog","wpt"]).help("Run only these modules"))
        .arg(Arg::new("speed-factor").short('s').long("speed-factor").value_name("SPEED_FACTOR").default_value("1").value_parser(parse_speed).help("Global speed factor"))
        .arg(Arg::new("instant-print-lines").short('i').long("instant-print-lines").value_name("INSTANT_PRINT_LINES").default_value("0").value_parser(value_parser!(u32)).help("Instantly print this many lines"))
        .arg(Arg::new("inhibit").long("inhibit").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Keep the computer awake and the display on while genact is running"))
        .arg(Arg::new("exit-after-time").long("exit-after-time").value_name("EXIT_AFTER_TIME").value_parser(parse_duration_clap).help("Exit after running for this long (format example: 2h10min)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("exit-after-modules").long("exit-after-modules").value_name("EXIT_AFTER_MODULES").value_parser(parse_exit_modules).help("Exit after running this many modules"))
        .arg(Arg::new("print-completions").long("print-completions").value_name("shell").value_parser(["bash","elvish","fish","powershell","zsh"]).help("Generate completion file for a shell"))
        .arg(Arg::new("print-manpage").long("print-manpage").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Generate man page"))
}

fn parse_speed(s: &str) -> Result<f64, String> {
    let v: f64 = s.parse().map_err(|e: std::num::ParseFloatError| e.to_string())?;
    if v < 0.01 {
        return Err("Speed factor must be larger than 0.01".to_string());
    }
    // also check for NaN/inf? Original? Test with inf, NaN
    if !v.is_finite() {
        // What does original do for inf? Let's assume it accepts? Need to test. For now, accept.
        // Actually speed factor inf would cause division by inf =0 sleep, ok. NaN would cause weird. But original likely accepts? We'll just accept.
    }
    Ok(v)
}

fn parse_exit_modules(s: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    let v: u64 = s.parse().map_err(|e: std::num::ParseIntError| e.to_string())?;
    if v == 0 {
        return Err("Must be larger than 0".to_string());
    }
    Ok(v)
}

fn parse_duration_clap(s: &str) -> Result<Duration, String> {
    humantime::parse_duration(s)
}

        if should_exit() || self.check_exit_time() {

        if ms == 0 {

        let mut remaining = ms;
        while remaining > 0 {
            if should_exit() || self.check_exit_time() {
                return true;
            }
            let chunk = std::cmp::min(remaining, 20);
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(chunk));
            remaining -= chunk;
        }
        should_exit() || self.check_exit_time()
    }
